facts.raw_span: a 5-year history of progressive, painless enlargement of her left breast
denied nipple discharge, skin changes, fever, weight loss, trauma, hormonal medication
no family history of breast cancer
menstrual cycles were regular
a well-defined, soft mass measuring 34×26×6 cm with dilated surface veins
the overlying skin, nipple, and areola were normal
no axillary lymphadenopathy
ultrasonography showed a homogeneously hyperechoic mass deep to the breast and pectoralis major muscle
mammography revealed a heterogeneous lucent mass in the left retromammary region involving the pectoralis muscle
magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a well-defined, homogeneous T1- and T2-hyperintense mass measuring approximately 15×13×10.2 cm
the clinical and imaging findings were consistent with a benign lesion
a core biopsy was not performed
